The Stack routine ran a full four-category mechanism sweep for the June 8–22 window, then applied the mandatory 21-day broadening (June 1–22). Zero mechanisms survived all seven gates. This is the tenth consecutive no-target cycle (June 12–22, 2026).

Validation Note

This is the tenth consecutive no-target cycle (June 12-22, 2026). The 14-day window (June 8-22) was applied first. The sole surviving candidate (FCC Second Submarine Cable SLTE Licensing Order) failed four independent gates upon live WebFetch verification: Gate 1 (both in-window editorial sources are law firm client advisories), Gate 3 (Thomas Sullivan's 2026 OIA Chief role unconfirmable; fcc.gov returns 503), Gate 4 (no fetchable source explicitly links Quintillion Arctic cable to Alaska AI data center connectivity), and Gate 5 (47 CFR confirms 5-member Commission is the decision body; no OIA Chief delegated authority found). The window was then broadened to 21 days (June 1-22) per protocol. DARPA-NSF AI Forge was the sole candidate in the June 1-7 extension — it failed Gates 1 (HPCwire returned HTTP 403), 4 (no Alaska AI consequence in any fetchable source), and 5 (program manager authority undocumented). A broad sweep of June 1-7 ANC news, NSF/UAF grants, and Alaska regulatory actions found no new qualifying mechanism. The dominant in-window news signal (FCC submarine cable reform) was covered exclusively by law firm client alerts, not by independent trade editorial. The Alaska AI consequence for fiber infrastructure remains inferential rather than explicitly documented. The bar was not lowered. An honest no-target is the correct outcome for this cycle.

Editor's Note

Run summary: Four scouts ran in parallel (facilities, vehicles, capital_sovereignty, regulatory). All four returned no viable candidates that survived the full 7-gate check. The closest candidate — the FCC Second Submarine Cable SLTE Licensing Order — fell on Gates 1, 3, 4, and 5 when the mapper WebFetched the alleged “editorial” sources and found they were law firm client advisories. The 21-day broadening was applied per protocol; DARPA-NSF AI Forge (the only June 1–7 candidate) failed Gates 1, 4, and 5 when HPCwire URLs returned HTTP 403 and no Alaska-specific AI consequence appeared in any fetchable source.

Structural pattern: The dominant in-window news signal for Alaska AI infrastructure (FCC submarine cable reform, FERC RM26-4 large-load orders) is being covered exclusively by law firm client alerts rather than by independent trade editorial. This is a genuine coverage gap for the category, not a mechanism gap. If a trade outlet (Defense News, Broadband Breakfast, Alaska Journal of Commerce) runs an original editorial on the FCC SLTE order's Alaska implications in the coming week, the mechanism may qualify in a future cycle.
